cohort: Pregnant women undergoing either elective (150) or non-elective (150) caesarean sections were included in the study.
finding: Positive uterine and placental cultures were significantly higher in women undergoing non-elective caesarean sections (21.33% and 12.00% respectively) compared to elective caesarean sections (8.67% and 5.33% respectively), with non-elective cases also showing substantially more puerperal infections and neonatal sepsis.
mod_finding: Non-elective caesarean section was associated with a higher incidence of positive uterine and placental cultures, puerperal infection, and neonatal sepsis compared to elective caesarean section, leading to the conclusion that counseling patients for elective caesarean section prior to labour onset might be beneficial.
